messages.author: 31c1235796669f0b
messages.subject: Using pdf() to export plot
parts:
Hi,

I tried to plot my graphics in a pdf, but using ggplot() left the pdf
empty.

pdf("test.pdf")
for(i in 1:3){
# I'll try to make three pages
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
}
dev.off()


Etienne

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Using pdf() to export plot
parts:
It's the loop: you need to explicitly print() the plot.
Hadley

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Using pdf() to export plot
parts:
Hi,

like lattice plots, you need to explicitly call print within a loop,

try

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) + geom_point()
print(p)
}
dev.off()

baptiste

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: Using pdf() to export plot
parts:
Here's an example of adding text, does this help?

text <- data.frame(x = 20, y = 25, label = 'test')
ggplot(aes(x = dist, y = speed), data = cars) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(x = x, y = y, label = label), data = text)

Cheers
david.
